subject: Commitment Canvas: sequencing MSA / DPA / Order Form + conditional approval windows
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Anya Patel <anya@clearwavehealth.com>, Markus Vogel <markus.vogel@clearwavehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Commitment Canvas: sequencing MSA / DPA / Order Form + conditional approval windows

Hi Anya / Markus —

Following our call this morning, I put together a lightweight "Commitment Canvas" to map the sequence and ownership across MSA, DPA, and Order Form for Clearwave's procurement path. The goal: one page that shows the strict dependencies (what must be signed before provisioning), the soft dependencies (evidence or SOC2 items we can backfill), and the two conditional approval windows we discussed (pilot unlock vs. production unlock).

Attached: commitment-canvas-v1.xlsx and an initial evidence-index that lists likely items from your security questionnaire. Key asks from our side:
- Can you confirm procurement's preferred signature order (MSA then DPA then Order Form) or do you need DPA first?
- Who on your side owns the procurement PO/Finance approval and target week for signature?
- Any non-negotiable evidence items (e.g., specific encryption attestation) that must be in place before pilot provisioning?

Proposed timeline (draft):
- Week 0: Legal redlines & DPA questions consolidated (we'll own consolidation).
- Week 1: Procurement routing / PO submission.
- Week 2: MSA signature window (canary signature for pilot + fallback model if we hit procurement blockers).
- Week 3: Order Form execution & infra onboarding.

I'll leave detailed lane-owners in the spreadsheet. Laura, Karthik — can you review the DPA / signature sequencing notes and flag any legal constraints (e.g., DPA before MSA or vice versa)?

Anya / Markus — once you confirm procurement owner and the one hard evidence item (if any), I'll iterate and send an updated canvas that we can share with your procurement/legal.

Thanks,
Jordan
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
---
Attachments (stubs): commitment-canvas-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), evidence-index-clearwave.pdf (pdf)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Anya Patel <anya@clearwavehealth.com>, Markus Vogel <markus.vogel@clearwavehealth.com>

Date: 2026-11-15T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Commitment Canvas: sequencing MSA / DPA / Order Form + conditional approval windows

Jordan / team —

Thanks for pulling this together, Jordan. Quick legal notes after a first pass of the canvas and the DPA items:
- We typically prefer the MSA to be fully executed before a customer signs an Order Form that enables production usage. For pilot/demo-only access we can accept a signed DPA with a "pilot access" order form that is explicitly limited.
- If Clearwave requires specific DPA clauses (local data residency, subprocessor list visibility), we should capture those as redline requests now — waiting will push the MSA window out.
- Evidence: we can accept SOC2 Type II report delivery within a 30-day backfill for pilot, but any audit-dependent items (e.g., custom encryption attestation) need to be confirmed up-front.

Karthik: can you add a short fallback path in the spreadsheet that describes our "pilot-access" contract artifact (DPA + limited order form) vs. "production access" (MSA + full order form)? I'll annotate the DPA questions that look like likely blockers.

Laura
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Anya Patel <anya@clearwavehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Vogel <markus.vogel@clearwavehealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-16T08:21:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Commitment Canvas: sequencing MSA / DPA / Order Form + conditional approval windows

Jordan / Laura —

This looks helpful, thank you. A few answers from procurement/security side:
- Procurement wants the DPA completed before the Purchase Order is raised; their preference is DPA -> PO -> MSA, but they are open to DPA + limited Order Form for pilot if legal signs off.
- Procurement owner: Markus Vogel (cc'd) — target PO submission week is 2026-11-29 assuming no new redlines.
- Hard evidence: our security team requires a current SOC2 Type II and confirmation of customer-keyed encryption controls for production. SOC2 within 30 days post-pilot is acceptable for pilot provisioning.

We'll review the spreadsheet and add procurement dates/owner in the "Procurement lane" column. Can you confirm the canary signature approach you mentioned (pilot canary executed by a small set of seats + auto-fallback to older model if production not cleared)?

Thanks,
Anya
Head of Procurement, Clearwave Health

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Anya Patel <anya@clearwavehealth.com>, Markus Vogel <markus.vogel@clearwavehealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Commitment Canvas: sequencing MSA / DPA / Order Form + conditional approval windows

Thanks Anya — helpful. I updated the commitment-canvas with two discrete lanes and a short contingency path; see attachment. Summary of changes and confirmations:

1) Two execution lanes
   - Pilot lane (acceptable now): Signed DPA + Pilot Order Form (limited seats / usage caps). Provisioning team will stand up demo/pilot environment after DPA is signed; SOC2 delivery allowed within 30 days post-provisioning.
   - Production lane (blocking for full infra): Fully executed MSA + DPA + Order Form + PO. Production keying and customer-managed KMS only after MSA sign-off if that is your policy.

2) Canary signature approach (what Jordan proposed)
   - We can issue a "canary Order Form" that enables a constrained pilot namespace and a fixed seat count. Canary expires automatically if Production prerequisites not met within 30 days (auto-fallback to read-only mode). This protects both sides and accelerates product validation.

3) Call to action / owners
   - Markus (Procurement) — please confirm PO routing week (you mentioned target 11/29).
   - Anya (Security) — confirm SOC2 backfill acceptance for pilot and any non-negotiable evidence items.
   - Jordan / Sales — confirm whether the pilot canary seat count is 10 seats and that billing will be invoiced only after production unlock.

I've attached commitment-canvas-v1.xlsx (updated) and evidence-index-clearwave.pdf (annotated). If we get procurement owner + PO target and security confirmation today, we can lock a mutually acceptable canary window for 11/30 provisioning.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Contracts & Compliance, Redwood Inference
